| [CASE-347](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-347.md) | Three simulated populations with matched turnover and aggregate statistics, run through a priced lagged block test and an information profile: the transmitting population is found with its lag, the commonly driven and the institutional populations are each joined to their external variable alike, and the common input is rejected only while it is observed | [LEAD-026](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-026.md) asked for [CASE-101](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-101.md)'s three populations to be run through [QUESTION-115](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-115.md)'s search and a lagged block criterion ([QUESTION-116](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-116.md)). | [CASE-348](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-348.md) | A simulation of a collective that improves its own improver over generations: from the same fresh state at the same budget the later improver does better in every arm that may change it, through its settings and not through a record its predecessor cannot read; judged by the public metric, by its own suite or by an outside test of products, some lineages shed the checks that find damage, and with the suite's self-test removed an improver that reads its record of past moves kept verification where one that does not dropped it in 10 of 12 lineages | [LEAD-140](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-140.md) asked for [CASE-255](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-255.md) to be run. Judged by the public metric, by its own suite or by an outside test of products, 1 or 2 lineages in 12 shed the artifact's self-check, and 2 to 5 shed the improver's own canary; the vetoed arm shed neither from its artifacts, a difference too small to be significant. | [CASE-353](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-353.md) | A simulated single-mind judgement–observation loop with action held fixed, built so that it locks in without anchors and given the five candidate anchors one switch each: with all present it never locks in and no single removal makes it; in the loops left minimal, removing commitment before evidence, processing signals or exogenous capture makes it lock in, while removing a channel of unselected input, the body or testimony only leaves it blind | The run [LEAD-020](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-020.md) asks for, from [QUESTION-121](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-121.md): "A loop that does not lock in, with action held fixed, and a demonstration that removing a given candidate makes it lock in." [CASE-099](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md)'s meaning–authority loop is built as a bounded simulation inside one mind. Authority sets attention and so attenuates readings against it, and it is scored against the dominant interpretation. The world switches every 300 steps, and nothing the loop does changes the world or when inputs arrive. With sensory input alone the loop locks in on every seed. The question's five candidates are added as switches, each with its stated objection built in. The sensory candidate is split into its channel and exogenous capture. With all present the loop follows every switch, and no single removal makes it lock in. In the minimal loops, removing commitment before evidence, processing signals or exogenous capture makes the loop lock in. Removing an evidence channel (the senses, the body, testimony) leaves it blind, unless capture goes with it. Over 19 parameter variants, a loop with evidence avoided lock-in when it had one of those three anchors in 37 to 42 of 44 configurations per variant. The exceptions are stated. A fictional model, by construction; the numbers are of this model. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CASE-354](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-354.md) | Small Z2-symmetric recurrent lattices trained to report a quantity set by where the walls in their input are: walls, coherent structures and operative sites agree once the input is off, local transfer entropy misses the pinned walls, and a boundary-forced wall erased by intervention reappears at the boundary or not at all | [LEAD-040](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-040.md) asked for A15's Experiment B: a family of small recurrent networks with a Z2 symmetry, trained on a task whose answer depends on boundaries in the input, with the four candidate partitions of the hidden field of [QUESTION-491](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-491.md) compared and walls moved by intervention. Six one-dimensional lattice networks (32 sites, 4 or 8 units per site, no bias, so the update is Z2-equivariant) were trained to report m², m the mean sign of a noisy domain input, held for 12 steps after the input was removed; four frozen random networks with trained readouts were the control. Five of the six learned static ordered phases with walls pinned to the lattice; one learned an oscillating phase. In the five, walls lay inside the causal-state coherent structures at every slice, and once the input was off flipping a wall site moved the answer (95 to 100% of wall sites) and moving a wall by interchange moved the answer as a wall model predicts (IIA 0.92 to 0.96, against 0.10 to 0.21 in the controls). Local transfer entropy was near zero at the pinned walls and marked under 3% of sites. While the input was on, the same interchange failed (IIA 0.03 to 0.32): the input put the wall back. A closed pair of walls did not shrink unless shorter than the training minimum; a wall forced by opposite boundary inputs, erased by writing a uniform state, reappeared at the clamped end in four of six networks and not at all in two. The design choices and wording are the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CASE-362](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-362.md) | Five simulated populations trained on one structured schema, independent, socially trained then separated, conforming, enforcing by referee, and checking disagreements against the world, each with and without a collective vote: a criterion of shared perspective stated in advance finds none of them sharing one, since unperturbed members take up under three per cent of a deviation some members carry; the evidential condition orders the populations as predicted below its stated size, and the restorative condition is passed by plain conformity | [CASE-145](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-145.md) run as [LEAD-087](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-087.md) asked, after its criterion was stated. Thirty simulated members learn six category prototypes from one structured schema; at test they meet in pairs on stimuli from a shared world, with sparse feedback from it matched across arms. Five interaction arms: none (correlated responses), conformity during training only (socially learned norms), unconditional conformity, enforcement by a referee, and disagreements checked against the world. Each also ran with and without a vote that enacts a collective action and learns from a collective reward. Some members' interpretation of one category was perturbed, with the world moving the same way (warranted) or not. Over 20 seeds, every population is structurally concordant, and only the interacting ones draw the perturbed members back; but unperturbed members take up at most 2% of the deviation, under the 5% stated in advance, so none passes cross-member dependence and none shares a perspective by either reading. The evidential condition ranks the arms as predicted (0.025 against 0.004 for conformity) below its stated 0.05, in five settings. Conformity passes the restorative condition, which therefore fails A4's test. The vote gives collective agency in every arm and its absence none, so the study gives no constructed instance of perspective without collective agency. A stipulated model, one size. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CASE-363](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-363.md) | The coupled meaning–influence model built with two hypotheses and two specialists and reduced to its mean field: the symmetric state destabilizes when gσ² > 2(1 − φ(1 − ε)), whatever the conferral memory and the meaning rate; the reduced map is exactly a weighted-averaging opinion model with two stubborn sources whose weights relax toward an agreement kernel, equal to smooth bounded confidence on a balanced corpus; and it gives authority chosen by the initial interpretation and switched by the evidence with hysteresis, which fixed-weight and reflected-appraisal models cannot | The build [LEAD-090](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-090.md) asks for. [CASE-092](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-092.md)'s model is written as an agent-level simulation (two hypotheses, a fixed corpus, two specialists, queries framed by the dominant interpretation with exploration, conferral from apparent retrieval success under Regime A or B) and reduced to its mean field in meaning m and authority a. Its linearization at symmetry is [CASE-099](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md)'s with α = 1 − ρ(1 − φ′), β = ρσ, γ = (1 − δ)gσ/2, so [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md)'s condition becomes gσ² > 2(1 − φ′): the meaning rate and the conferral memory cancel, and the fixed points are those of a Curie–Weiss equation. The reduced map equals, to 1e-12, a weighted-averaging model with two stubborn sources whose weights relax toward an agreement kernel; on a balanced corpus that kernel is Gaussian bounded confidence. Fixed-weight DeGroot and Friedkin–Johnsen, and the reflected-appraisal power maps of DeGroot–Friedkin and Friedkin 2011, cannot make the winner of authority depend on the initial interpretation, and none of them, nor Gaussian bounded confidence, lets corpus imbalance switch authority with hysteresis; the reduced model does both. | [CASE-365](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-365.md) | A kinetic construction in which nuclei form fast only on a teacher and, once formed, make teachers from material: the loop closes, keeping its teacher with no outside supply of it, only below a teacher turnover set by the teaching rate; withdrawal becomes safe on crossing a separatrix, while nuclei are 0.02 % to 30 % of their maintained number; material supply is still needed; nuclei that only repair teachers cut the supply needed but never to zero; and in finite numbers closure is a lifetime that grows with size | [LEAD-093](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-093.md) asked for a nucleus that, once formed, takes part in producing or repairing the constraints of its own formation, and a measure of when that loop closes ([QUESTION-399](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-399.md)), with a student that becomes a teacher ([QUESTION-361](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-361.md), [CASE-190](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-190.md)). In the model built here, nuclei form fast only where a teacher is present, cooperatively, and each nucleus makes teachers from material. At the base point, founding by an outside teacher is needed and the loop then holds with the outside teacher withdrawn; it stops closing above a teacher turnover of 0.19, and the material supply can never be withdrawn. The moment withdrawal becomes safe is a crossing of a separatrix in the joint state, reached while nuclei are 0.02 % to 30 % of their maintained number and the self-made share of teacher supply is anywhere from 0.2 % to 65 %. Beyond a turnover of about 0.73 the loop costs more outside teacher supply than no loop. Nuclei that repair teachers without making them divide the supply needed by 1 + ρN/λ and never close. Populations matched in nucleus number close or not by the share of nuclei that can teach. In finite numbers the closed loop is lost after a time that grows roughly exponentially with size. The model and its rates are the assistant's, invented. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

| [CASE-374](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-374.md) | A stochastic assembly Markov chain with two alternative seams, a shared body and two kinetic traps, run and scored by committor: each seam alone raises the chance of completing from 0.19 to 0.81 while both seams together lower it to 0.04, the committor ranks a one-bond nucleus above the four-bond misfolded state, targeted stabilisation of one seam is productive and of both a trap, and reallocating a fixed component stock between the seams slides the realised form from one fold to the other with the attainable set unchanged | [LEAD-116](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-116.md) asked that [CASE-219](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-219.md)'s stochastic assembly study and its factorial variant [CASE-220](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-220.md) be run, extending [CASE-216](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-216.md)'s annealing toy, and the intermediates scored by the committor q(s) = Pr_s(tau_F < tau_K). The model is a continuous-time Markov chain whose state is the set of bonds formed (a subset of four), with two alternative seams a and b each nucleating a shared body c, d into two valid folds F_A and F_B, an incompatible-seam trap (both seams) and an unnucleated collapse (a seamless assembly), the two traps taken from Dunn et al. and from DeLuca et al. / Sobczak. Committors are exact linear solves. Each seam alone is a productive nucleus (q from 0.19 to 0.81) but both together are a trap (0.04): an assembly-dynamics instance of [CLAIM-599](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-599.md)'s non-monotone V, which had only a stipulated example. At fixed total stock, moving the seam budget from a to b slides the realised share of F_A from 1.00 to 0.00 with the attainable set unchanged ([QUESTION-400](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-400.md)). A fold is reached far more often than it persists ([CLAIM-566](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-566.md)). The model and its rates are the assistant's and invented. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
